name: 林鷸
illustrationTaxon: Tringa glareola, monotypic: 19-23 cm. A small to medium-sized shorebird, similar to Green Sandpiper but distinguished by its habitual occurrence in flocks, paler brown upperparts with larger pale spotting, paler and more diffuse chest colouration, a diffuse supercilium behind the eye and more yellowish legs. The adult in breeding plumage has coarse whitish and buff marks on the upperparts; the juvenile is neatly spotted above with paler underparts and a finely streaked breast; the adult winter is greyer with a plainer chest and flanks. In flight it is distinguished from Green Sandpiper by narrow tail bars, paler brown upperparts with more whitish spots and thus less uniform, and pale underwings.

similarSpecies.distinction: 白腰草鷸常單獨出現，背部深褐近黑而對比強烈、胸腹的暗色濃而集中，眉紋在眼後就斷掉，腳偏灰綠；本種成群出現，背部較淡的褐色佈滿較大的白點、胸前只是淡淡一抹灰，眉紋延伸到眼後，腳偏黃。
小黃腳鷸體型較大、後半身拖得更長，頭頂沒有一頂深色帽，背上的白色缺口較細密，腳是明亮的純黃色；本種體型小一號、背上是較大的白點，腳偏黃綠。

featureNotes: 嘴中等長度、直而深色，比澤鷸那一類「針嘴」短得多，也沒有青腳鷸微微上翹的弧度（第1圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
白色眉紋由眼先一直延伸到眼後、邊緣柔和；這正是與白腰草鷸的分別之一（後者眉紋在眼後就斷掉）（第2圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
背部是較淡的褐色，撒滿一顆顆清楚的白點，整體比白腰草鷸的深黑褐背雜亂得多——HKBWS 用「larger pale spotting」形容（第3圈取自全身圖，實際可見）。
腿長而呈黃綠色（偏黃而非偏灰綠），成群在淡水濕地的淺水與濕泥上覓食（第4圈取自全身圖，實際可見）。

sources.use: HKBWS substantive read: Category I, a common migrant and winter visitor to freshwater wetlands with some evidence of a decline in numbers; 19-23 cm, a small to medium-sized shorebird similar to Green Sandpiper but distinguished by habitual occurrence in flocks, paler brown upperparts with larger pale spotting, paler and more diffuse chest colouration, a diffuse supercilium behind the eye and more yellowish legs; the adult in breeding plumage has coarse whitish and buff marks on the upperparts, the juvenile is neatly spotted above with paler underparts and a finely streaked breast, and the adult winter is greyer with a plainer chest and flanks; in flight it is distinguished from Green Sandpiper by narrow tail bars, paler brown upperparts with more whitish spots and thus less uniform, and pale underwings; the typical flight call of flushed birds is a fairly loud repeated too or tyee, with a double-note contact-alarm call when alert or agitated; it occurs in low-lying areas of freshwater and brackish marsh, wet agriculture, fish ponds, larger channelised watercourses and rice paddy throughout the New Territories, especially at Long Valley (highest count 221), Kam Tin (190) and previously the San Tin-Lok Ma Chau-Chau Tau area (300) and the former Kai Tak airport (164), and is regularly recorded on Lantau and Po Toi in generally low numbers, with small numbers on the Deep Bay intertidal mudflats especially during spring passage though this is not the preferred habitat and it is very rarely seen there in winter; it is a common passage migrant and winter visitor with highest numbers in autumn, autumn passage generally noted from the second week of July with main passage from the second week of August to the end of October peaking around the beginning of that month and the highest numbers in 1998 reaching 1,221 on 10 September, the highest since then being 597 on 9 October 2006; winter numbers are relatively constant from the third week of November to mid-February with the highest counts 350 on 25 January 1992 and 200 on 24 January 1977 and 8 January 2007; spring passage commences in March with numbers increasing to a peak in the third week of April, the highest single-site counts being 450 on 12 April 1990 and 14 April 2002 and a total of 452 at four sites on 14 April 1996, numbers declining sharply at the end of April and the species becoming rare by the second week of May, while June sees the fewest records with generally no more than four; Vaughan and Jones (1913) called it a common passage migrant often occurring in large flocks frequenting both the coast and the country inland from 21 August to 5 May, and Macfarlane and Macdonald (1966) knew it as a regular passage migrant with up to 250 birds in spring and 50 in autumn mainly from the paddy areas of the northwest New Territories with extreme dates 1 February to 22 May and 27 July to 27 December; Herklots (1967) commented that it was mainly recorded in paddy areas, which are now rare in HK, and there appears to have been a decline associated with this, with relatively high counts in the late 1960s and early 1970s at a time of much lower observer activity than the 1990s supporting such an interpretation and numbers reported in autumn since 2010 appearing consistently lower than in the 20 years prior; it is a characteristic bird of freshwater and brackish wetland areas with small groups readily flying up and calling when flushed, foraging in shallow water or wet mud by pecking at the water or mud surface and sweeping the bill through the water; monotypic, breeding from northern and central Europe east through Russia, northern Kazakhstan, northern Mongolia and northeast China to Kamchatka, and wintering in sub-Saharan Africa, parts of the Middle East, the Indian subcontinent, south China, Indochina, southeast Asia and Indonesia to Australia; in China it breeds in the northwest and northeast and winters along the south coast including Hainan and Taiwan; IUCN Least Concern with a stable population trend.

notes: AI 生成插圖，經人眼核對中等長度深色嘴、延伸到眼後的柔和眉紋、密佈白點的褐背及黃綠色長腿；單型種。
兩隻比較鳥均為 AI 生成示意（白腰草鷸沿用 0163 已核對的全身圖、小黃腳鷸沿用 0169 已核對的全身圖），非等比例；卡上不作完整鑑別檢索表。
全身圖沿用 0164 已核對的林鷸圖（同一物種、同一批插圖風格），本卡只新繪近景圖；兩張圖的白點密度與色調一致。
慣常成群是與白腰草鷸最實用的野外分別，但「成群」拍不進單隻鳥的圓圈，所以第 3、4 圈改為呈現背部白點與腿色，並在說明寫明。
飛行時的窄尾斑、較淡且較多白點的背、偏白的翼下——這些要在飛行中才看得清，卡面只放靜態站姿。
IUCN 無危 LC（趨勢穩定）；香港屬 Category I，是淡水濕地常見的過境鳥與越冬鳥，但與稻田消失有關，數量有下降跡象，秋季數量自 2010 年起持續偏低。
地圖為 Natural Earth 110m 世界底圖的國家層級概述，不是精確分佈多邊形，繁殖地與越冬地不分工。
